problem: Complex multi-hop queries over domain-specific KGs need retrieval that aligns semantic reasoning with structured traversal; plain RAG and GraphRAG retrieval are weaker on mid-complexity multi-hop queries.
method: GraphTrace: a modular retrieval framework over a domain-specific KG (COVID-19 economic data) with entity extraction, path finding, query decomposition, semantic path ranking, and context aggregation, followed by LLM-based answer generation.
key_assumptions: Decomposing queries and ranking semantic paths yields better context than flat RAG/graph RAG.
A domain-specific KG (COVID-19 economic data) is a representative testbed. [abstract]
main_contribution: A modular KG+LLM retrieval framework whose components (path finding, query decomposition, semantic path ranking, context aggregation) improve retrieval and generation over RAG and GraphRAG baselines, with particular gains on 5-6-hop queries.
datasets: Structured economic data related to the COVID-19 pandemic (domain-specific KG) [abstract]
benchmarks: In-domain COVID-19 economic multi-hop query set (specific benchmark names not stated in the abstract)
metrics: Retrieval metrics (unspecified in abstract) and generation metrics including 'directness'
results: GraphTrace consistently outperforms RAG and GraphRAG baselines, especially on mid-complexity (5-6-hop) queries, and achieves top 'directness' scores in the generation evaluation.
limitations: Inference-time retrieval only; no model training, no supervision-design comparison, no repair or RL.
Domain-specific (COVID-19 economic) evaluation; exact metrics, dataset size, and error analysis not stated in the abstract.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: GraphTrace is an inference-time retrieval pipeline (query decomposition, path ranking, context aggregation) over a domain KG; it neither fine-tunes the LLM on triple/path supervision nor attaches same-passage context to a training target, and has no repair or RL. Its relevance is as a context-aggregation baseline for multi-hop retrieval rather than an overlapping supervision method.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.5 because both concern multi-hop QA over KGs with context aggregation and hop-depth effects (GraphTrace reports gains at 5-6 hops, related to the idea's H4); method overlap 0.3 because retrieval/path ranking is shared in spirit but there is no training-signal design, no context-graph supervision, no repair, and no RL; evaluation overlap 0.35 because both use multi-hop accuracy-like measures but on different, unspecified benchmarks and metrics.
